key_insight: Spanwise mean-flow skew reduces the magnitude of mixing-layer statistics, but the turbulent shear-layer dynamics and self-similar structure remain largely intact.
engineering_relevance: For 3D shear-flow devices and models, moderate mean-flow skew can change performance levels without fundamentally altering the mixing-layer growth law or stress-shape behavior.
method: Generated skewed mixing layers with turning vanes near the splitter-plate trailing edge
Measured downstream velocity fields using cross-wire anemometry
Compared planar vs skewed cases using similarity scaling, shear-layer thickness, Reynolds stresses, and Townsend’s structure parameter
evidence_signal: Across the experiments, skewed cases showed systematic reductions in mean and turbulent quantities of up to about 40%, while similarity collapse, near-linear thickness growth, and near-Gaussian stress profiles were preserved.
watch_item: The result is experimentally specific to the tested skewing method and flow conditions, so broader 3D shear-flow designs may not preserve the same invariances.
paper_title: Effects of mean flow skew on turbulent shear layers. Part II. Experimental investigation
